title: MIND (La Mente)
description: Exploring topics about happiness, the internet's impact on the brain, and intelligence.

grammar.title: Articles (a/an/the/no article)
grammar.rule: Use 'the' with specific things, use 'a/an' with general things, use no article for general uncountable nouns.
grammar.example: I go to school (as a student) vs I go to the school (the building). The happiness I feel is real. A good book can change your perspective.
tips: Use 'the' before unique places: the brain, the internet
Phrases: go to school (student), go to the school (building)

grammar.title: Used to
grammar.rule: Express habits or states in the past that no longer occur now.
grammar.example: I used to feel anxious all the time. She used to spend hours on social media. We used to think intelligence was only about IQ.
tips: Common with emotions: used to feel, used to think

categories.name: Sentimientos
categories.description: Emotions and feelings related to happiness and well-being

words.example: She felt a deep sadness after the loss.
He found contentment in simple things.
Career fulfillment is important to many people.
Exercise gives me peace of mind.

categories.name: Phrasal Verbs
categories.description: Phrasal verbs related to emotions and mental states

words.example: He cheered up when he saw his friends.
Take a deep breath and calm down.
Don't freak out about the exam.
I need to figure out what makes me happy.
How do you deal with stress?

exercises.title: Past Habits Reflection
exercises.description: Write about your habits and feelings from the past
exercises.instructions: Write 5-7 sentences about what you used to do, think, or feel that is different now. Include at least 3 'used to' structures and correct articles.
exercises.example: I used to think that money was the only way to be happy. When I was younger, I used to spend all my time on the internet. Now I realize that real connections matter more than likes. The happiness I feel today comes from different places than it did before.

exercises.title: Your Brain & The Internet
exercises.description: Analyze how the internet affects your brain and mind
exercises.instructions: Write 6-8 sentences about how the internet has changed your thinking patterns, memory, or emotions. Use articles correctly when mentioning specific things (the internet, the brain, etc.)
exercises.example: The internet has changed the way my brain works. I used to read books for hours, but now I scroll through content quickly. The constant notifications affect my concentration. An article I read explained how this impacts the prefrontal cortex of the brain.

exercises.title: Intelligence Redefined
exercises.instructions: Write 7-10 sentences about what intelligence means to you beyond just IQ. Use various article structures and describe what you used to think vs what you think now.
exercises.example: I used to believe that intelligence was only measured by test scores. Now I understand that there are many types of intelligence. The emotional intelligence I've developed is as important as academic knowledge. People who have practical intelligence can solve real problems. A truly intelligent person combines different skills and perspectives.

dialogues.title: Coffee Shop Conversation About Happiness
dialogues.situation: Two friends discussing what makes them happy

conversation.speaker: Alex
conversation.text: I used to think happiness was about having money and success.

conversation.speaker: Jordan
conversation.text: Yeah, but then you realize the simple things matter more, right?

conversation.speaker: Alex
conversation.text: Exactly! The real happiness comes from relationships and personal growth.

conversation.speaker: Jordan
conversation.text: I couldn't agree more. I used to worry about everything, but now I focus on what I can control.

dialogues.title: Discussing Internet Habits
dialogues.situation: A parent and teenager talking about internet use

conversation.speaker: Parent
conversation.text: You used to spend more time outside. Now you're always on your phone.

conversation.speaker: Teen
conversation.text: I know, but the internet helps me stay connected with friends.

conversation.speaker: Parent
conversation.text: Connection is important, but face-to-face interaction is different.

conversation.speaker: Teen
conversation.text: You're right. I used to enjoy outdoor activities more.

practice_activities.title: Articles and Used to Practice
practice_activities.instructions: Fill in the blanks with 'a', 'an', 'the', or leave blank (Ø) if no article is needed.
sentences: I ___ used to feel anxious, but now I practice meditation.
The ___ happiness I feel today is different from ___ happiness in the past.
___ School is important for learning, but I also learned a lot outside ___ school.
He has ___ intelligence that helps him solve complex problems.
She used to spend ___ hour on ___ internet every day.

questions.question: I ___ enjoy reading, but now I prefer watching videos.
The ___ brain is affected by ___ internet usage.

study: Research: 'The science of happiness' - find 3 interesting facts
Watch: A TED talk about intelligence or happiness (with subtitles)
Read: An article about how social media affects the brain
Compare: Your own internet habits from 5 years ago vs now
Analyze: Different types of intelligence (emotional, practical, analytical)
practice: Write 15 sentences using 'used to' + 5 different emotions
Create 10 examples of 'the' vs no article with school, home, hospital
Make sentences with 6 different phrasal verbs from the vocabulary
Record yourself speaking about past habits (use 'used to')
Interview someone about what they used to believe vs what they believe now
write: Paragraph: How your thinking has changed over the years
Reflection: What made you happy as a child vs now
Opinion: Is intelligence more important than happiness?
Analysis: How the internet has impacted your intelligence and mood

tips: ARTICLES: 'go to school' = as a student, 'go to the school' = the building
USED TO: Only for past, negative is 'didn't use to', question is 'Did you use to...?'
THE: Use with unique things, but NOT with general plural nouns
PHRASAL VERBS: Remember they are verbs + prepositions, keep them together
PRONUNCIATION: Practice the difference between 'used to' (you-st-to) and 'use to' (use-to)
CONTEXT: 'Used to' shows change - what was true before is not true now
prompts: What did you use to believe about success that you don't believe anymore?
How have your feelings about the internet changed over time?
What type of intelligence do you think you have the most of?
Write about a time when you had to deal with anxiety or stress
What habits have you successfully changed? How did you do it?
Do you think artificial intelligence will change human happiness? Why?
